subject: Unearthed clip exposes how far Talarico was willing to go on raising taxes during COVID era
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Unearthed clip exposes how far Talarico was willing to go on raising taxes during COVID era

James Talarico once said he didn't care what taxes had to be raised to avoid healthcare cuts in Texas during the COVID-19 budget shortfalls.

Actual Article Body:
This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten, or redistributed. ©2026 FOX News Network, LLC. All rights reserved. Quotes displayed in real-time or delayed by at least 15 minutes. Market data provided by Factset. Powered and implemented by FactSet Digital Solutions. Legal Statement. Mutual Fund and ETF data provided by LSEG.

Texas Democratic U.S. Senate nominee James Talarico discusses his controversial past statements, explains his stance on border security and more on 'Special Report.'

James Talarico, the Democratic nominee for the Senate in Texas, once pressed Democrats to consider cuts to healthcare benefits a nonstarter — regardless of the consequences for the state’s finances.

The remark came during a podcast interview in which Talarico discussed how Texas might balance its budget amid COVID-related shortfalls. He feared Republicans would look for savings in healthcare services.

"I don't care where you get the revenue. I don't care what taxes you have to raise," Talarico said in a 2020 appearance with Texas Rising, a progressive YouTube channel focused on political engagement among younger voters.

The resurfaced moment adds to the pile of past statements dealing with gender, immigration and fiscal management, complicating the political calculus for Talarico as he aims to convince voters in Texas that he could represent a Republican-leaning constituency, even as a Democrat.

TALARICO SAYS HE 'MISSED THE MARK' AS HE BACKTRACKS ON CONTROVERSIAL WOKE STATEMENTS

Democrat candidate for Senate James Talarico speaks during a rally in San Antonio, Texas, on May 29, 2026. (Ronaldo Schemidt/AFP via Getty Images)

At the time, Texas was facing a bleak financial outlook.

The pandemic had crippled key sections of the state’s regular revenue streams. As oil demand crashed nationally, tax revenue that would normally come from hotels, bars and restaurants also faced steep reductions. Texas Comptroller Glenn Hegar projected a $4.6 billion shortfall.

"The economic contraction associated with COVID-19 has resulted in revenue collection this fiscal year that is much lower than our earlier projections," Hegar said in a statement.

"This estimate also assumes that restrictions on businesses and individuals will be lifted before the end of this calendar year and that economic activity will strengthen."

As a part of the COVID response, Texas ordered most agencies to look for ways to cut their spending by 5% in the 2020 – 2021 budget.

In a letter, Governor Greg Abbott largely shielded Health and Human Services (HHS) from the reductions, sparing the state’s Medicaid program, the Children’s Health Insurance Program, the foster care program and disability services, among others. Even so, $2.6 billion of HHS’s budget remained subject to cuts, according to the agency's estimations.

That left the Health and Human Services Commission with a target of $132,716,600 in cuts.

'FAKE' MODERATE TALARICO'S TEXAS SURGE TESTS PAXTON IN FIGHT TO HOLD CRUCIAL GOP SENATE SEAT

Democratic U.S. Senate candidate James Talarico speaks during a campaign rally at the Cailloux Theater on Aug. 31, 2026, in Kerrville, Texas. Talarico is campaigning across the state in a close race against Republican candidate and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton ahead of the Nov. 3 general election. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images)

Despite the reduced figure, Talarico blasted the idea of making spending reductions geared towards healthcare.

"You're not going to make our students and our teachers — you're not going to make the sick and the elderly pay for this pandemic we are not going to balance our budget off of the most vulnerable people in this state," Talarico said.

He argued that Democrats should create a similar kind of stigma against cuts to HHS as the one surrounding raising taxes.

"Sometimes you get the reaction in the capitol that's an unreasonable position to take. But the other side of the aisle has already taken revenue increases off the table. They've done a good job of making certain options taboo, so I think our coalition, not just Democrats but progressives, and anybody with a functioning heart should be able to make cuts to health and education taboo and take them off the table," Talarico said.

The moment has brought on criticisms from at least one Republican onlooker.

"High-tax Talarico never saw a tax hike he didn't love in the Texas Legislature, and he is promising to continue that if elected to the Senate. James Talarico will raise taxes on every Texan to fund his radical agenda of taxpayer-funded sex changes for kids and free healthcare for illegal immigrants," Zach Kraft, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

As he wages his bid for U.S. Senate, Talarico has advocated for an expansion of U.S. health policy.

On his website, Talarico has called for universal eligibility for Medicare, to regulate medical debt and expand veteran care. His views on Medicare, which overlap with many other progressives in the party, have prompted criticism from Republicans who believe such an expansion would cripple the federal budget with cost.

Skeptics of the plan have argued for years that such an expansion is too expensive and does little to address existing inefficiencies in the American healthcare system.

In 2019, Sen. John Barrasso, R-Wyo., took to the Senate floor to blast the idea, calling it a straitjacket solution that would undermine healthcare quality.

"The [Congressional Budget Office] projects in its report on a single-payer plan that government spending on health care would increase substantially. They go on to say to cover the massive cost of government-run care, income taxes would have to at least double. Income taxes, American families — at least double," Barrasso said.

SHOCK POLL: TALARICO TIES PAXTON IN TEXAS SENATE RACE, THREATENING GOP STRONGHOLD

Democratic Texas State Rep. James Talarico speaks during a campaign launch rally on Sept. 9, 2025, in Round Rock, Texas. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images)

Talarico’s campaign did not address questions on whether his designs for healthcare are shaped by the national deficit, but noted that his plan includes increases in taxes on the country's top earners.

"James supports making billionaires pay their fair share so we can cut taxes for middle class Texans and fund healthcare for working families — which is why he has unveiled plans to end special tax handouts to corporations and billionaires to help fund healthcare, while proudly voting for the largest property tax cut in Texas history to make sure middle class families get a break," the Talarico campaign told Fox News Digital. "Ken Paxton has worked to enrich himself and his billionaire mega-donors, amassed 15 properties on a taxpayer-funded salary, and was impeached by his own party for his corrupt abuse of office."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Having cleared the party primary, Talarico will face off against Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton in the state’s Nov. 3 general election.

Leo Briceno is a politics reporter for the congressional team at Fox News Digital. He was previously a reporter with World Magazine.

subject: GOP Senate hopeful sounds alarm after alleged Mall of America terror plot thwarted
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
GOP Senate hopeful sounds alarm after alleged Mall of America terror plot thwarted

Michele Tafoya says Minnesotans "feel under a level of threat" after the FBI arrested an 18-year-old over an alleged ISIS-inspired Mall of America plot.

Actual Article Body:
This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten, or redistributed. ©2026 FOX News Network, LLC. All rights reserved. Quotes displayed in real-time or delayed by at least 15 minutes. Market data provided by Factset. Powered and implemented by FactSet Digital Solutions. Legal Statement. Mutual Fund and ETF data provided by LSEG.

Republican U.S. Senate candidate Michele Tafoya is sounding the alarm about crime levels in the state amid a wave of Somali gang violence and a foiled terror plot by an American born to Somali parents.

Republican Senate nominee Michele Tafoya says people in her home state of Minnesota "feel under a level of threat" after the FBI arrested an 18-year-old who allegedly pledged allegiance to ISIS and discussed carrying out a mass shooting at the Mall of America.

Tafoya, who is aiming to flip a Democrat-controlled open Senate seat as she faces off against Democratic Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan in the midterm elections, praised authorities in an X post, writing, "Thank you to @FBIMinneapolis and law enforcement for stopping a potential mass-casualty attack."

But she also pointed to the midterms as she argued, "This November, the choice is clear: law and order or more of the same. Common sense or chaos."

Authorities said Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud had been under investigation for nearly two years before he was arrested on the spot after buying an AK-47-style rifle, magazines and ammunition from an undercover FBI employee.

FBI: MALL OF AMERICA TERROR PLOT THWARTED

"This was a radicalized young man who needed to be watched," U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen said Wednesday at a news conference. Rosen added that agents "were able to detect a threat and disrupt it before the defendant carried out his intention to kill, in his words, maybe 30 to 60 people."

Mohamud, according to an FBI agent's sworn complaint, repeatedly affirmed in chat messages to the informant that he intended to attack and kill non-Muslims at the mall on Oct. 24, the date of a scheduled Hmong arts celebration. The Hmong are an ethnic group from East and Southeast Asia with a large community in Minnesota."

Tafoya, in a Fox News Digital interview, said, "I hear a lot of concerns from Minnesotans on the campaign trail about crime, and no matter what form that crime takes, Minnesotans know that they feel under a level of threat that has increased lately here in Minnesota.

"And in the last week and just today, we saw the arrest of an 18-year-old ... American citizen to Somali parents arrested for ... planning a terrorist attack at the Mall of America," Tafoya said, as she referred not only to the thwarting of the terror plot, but also a recent spate of gang gun violence tied to what some in local law enforcement say are members of "the Somali American community."

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

"He basically stated that he wanted to take out anyone who was not a Muslim. He also noted that the Mall of America is owned by people who are Jewish," Tafoya added. "Again, he is of Somalian descent, and terror is alive and well. And thank God we averted this massive crisis."

Flanagan, in a statement on X, wrote, "I’m relieved that a horrific attack on Minnesota was prevented and grateful for the actions of law enforcement."

Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud, 18, was arrested after FBI officials say he pledged allegiance to ISIS and discussed carrying out a mass shooting at the Mall of America.  (U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota)

Fox News Digital reached out to Flanagan's campaign for more reaction to the terror plot arrest and to Tafoya's comments but didn't receive a response at the time this article was published.

Sen. Amy Klobuchar, the Democratic gubernatorial nominee, wrote in a statement, "I'm grateful for the heroic work of law enforcement that prevented a mass shooting and terrorist attack at the Mall of America. This shows why we continue to need major coordinated investments in anti-terrorism and local law enforcement to stop attacks like these."

MIDTERM MATH: THE THREE FORCES THAT COULD STOP A DEMOCRATIC BLUE WAVE

Klobuchar, who is running to succeed retiring Democratic Gov. Tim Walz, emphasized, "Our state must take terrorism and violent crime head on, working with our federal law enforcement and local police departments to keep Minnesotans safe."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Sen. Amy Klobuchar, D-Minn. (Bloomberg/Getty)

Her Republican rival in the gubernatorial showdown, House Speaker Lisa Demuth, also praised authorities.

"I’m grateful for the work of federal and local law enforcement that stopped this potentially catastrophic ISIS-inspired terrorist plot. It’s frightening to know that a young person could be led down this path," Demuth wrote on X.

"It’s fortunate that we have law enforcement officials and members of the U.S. Attorney’s Office that were able to do the work necessary to prevent a terrible act of mass violence from taking place in our community."

subject: 100-shot Somali gang gun battle rocks Minnesota as sheriff warns 'we're in trouble'
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
100-shot Somali gang gun battle rocks Minnesota as sheriff warns 'we're in trouble'

CCTV captured a gunfight that left 97 casings in Bloomington as Somali gang violence across Minnesota's Twin Cities draws national attention.

Actual Article Body:
This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten, or redistributed. ©2026 FOX News Network, LLC. All rights reserved. Quotes displayed in real-time or delayed by at least 15 minutes. Market data provided by Factset. Powered and implemented by FactSet Digital Solutions. Legal Statement. Mutual Fund and ETF data provided by LSEG.

Bloomington Chief Booker Hodges calls out Somali gangs as assimilation concerns rise following major automatic gunfire in local neighborhood. (Credit: KMSP)

Violence tied to Somali-American gangs in the Twin Cities metro erupted in recent days, with law enforcement recovering nearly 100 casings after a gunfight captured on a resident’s surveillance camera — as officials warn they need help to contain the problem before it escalates.

The warning follows a burst of violence across several Twin Cities suburbs — including a Bloomington shootout that left nearly 100 shell casings and another shooting in Eden Prairie — as law enforcement says the incidents have entered a retaliation cycle and officials race to disrupt the groups before the violence evolves into more entrenched drug- and money-driven crime.

"We have the opportunity to fix it," Ramsey County Sheriff Bob Fletcher said of a surge in Somali gang violence across the Twin Cities — but warned authorities could be facing a much more difficult problem if the groups escalate the resources they use.

3 DEAD, INCLUDING SUSPECTED GUNMAN, AND 3 OFFICERS INJURED IN MINNEAPOLIS SHOOTING

Bloomington Police chief Booker Hodges is seen at a press conference. (KMSP/FOX-9)

"It’s early. Once they evolve into drugs, we’re in trouble. Once they evolve into money, more money, we are in trouble," said Fletcher, whose county is anchored by St. Paul and runs along the west bank of the Mississippi River.

Fletcher estimated that about 300 juveniles are involved and said part of the problem lies in the Somali gangs’ relative novelty to local law enforcement and what he characterized as a reluctance to aggressively prosecute offenders across the river in Minneapolis.

TRUMP’S LAW-AND-ORDER BLITZ MARKS ONE YEAR WITH EYE-POPPING HAUL OF SUSPECTS, GUNS IN BLUE CITY

"We need more people focused on this problem. Because 50 kids in this 300 need to go to jail, 25 need to be prosecuted by the feds for RICO and and another 25 need to be prosecuted at the local level. Take 50 of the most active out of the mix, and we will see dramatic changes," he said.

He ascribed some of the reticence to neighboring Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty, saying she has not been sufficiently "aggressive" in prosecuting such offenders.

FEDERAL JUDGE REFERS PHILADELPHIA DA LARRY KRASNER TO DOJ FOR POSSIBLE CRIMINAL INVESTIGATION

"One of the misconceptions is that somehow when you prosecute people, put them in jail that you're destituting them to some terrible life. This is how kids get corrected," he said.

Moriarty’s office pushed back on the assertion, with spokesman Daniel Borgertpoepping saying the neighboring communities are "looking for solutions" and that Moriarty’s prosecutors "communicate daily with law enforcement [and] will participate in any group that moves us toward sustainable public safety."

A Ramsey County Sheriffs vehicle is shown. (Michael Siluk/Universal Images Group)

"The way we approach prosecution of violent crime is consistent regardless of the race or ethnicity of those involved," Borgertpoepping said.

Meanwhile, residents across the metro region expressed outrage to local officials over the violence and what they described as a growing threat to public safety.

Jared Scribner, a resident of nearby Edina, criticized officials for calling the issue "gun violence" and demanded they "confront what is happening even when the facts are politically uncomfortable."

Scribner said violence associated with the gangs erupted at a local homecoming event and at a park.

MEMPHIS MOM SAYS TRUMP BROUGHT PEACE TO STREETS AS DEMOCRATIC DA BATTLES TASK FORCE OVERSIGHT

The Minneapolis skyline, in and around where Somali gangs are cropping up, is seen. (Arthur Maiorella/Getty Images)

"We don't need more virtue signaling, yard signs, DEI initiatives, or community conversations that lead to nowhere. We need competent government, accountability, and safe neighborhoods," he said, also blaming Moriarty’s office for "refu[sing]" to properly address the issue.

He also suggested officials have sometimes generalized the ethnicity of those involved, remarking that it "feels more comfortable for some people to say East African. I don't even know that that's a fair term, because 98% of these gang members are Somalians."

In nearby Bloomington, where about 100 casings were recovered from the scene of a late-night firefight that appeared to involve automatic weapons, Police Chief Booker Hodges took a confrontational tack toward the suspects who remained at large — while warning they do not fit the typical stereotype of gang members.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

A street sign for "Somali St" is pictured with Riverside Plaza in the background in Minneapolis’ Cedar–Riverside neighborhood. (Michael Dorgan/Fox News Digital)

"They're coming from two parent homes, living in apartment buildings with $3,500 a month rent, driving Beamers and Mercedes. They're not dealing with money. There's no drugs in the house. They're purchasing legal firearms," he said.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"To those of you who did this shooting, you know that I know that you know that I that we know who you are. So my suggestion is: you turn yourself in. Let's stop playing these games with you running around out here doing all this stuff," Hodges warned — as the violence draws national attention.

subject: Iowa city council meeting erupts after former member opens meeting with satanic prayer
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Iowa city council meeting erupts after former member opens meeting with satanic prayer and 'Hail Satan'

A former Ottumwa City Council member opened a meeting with a satanic prayer ending in "Hail Satan," prompting a pastor to call the controversial incident a "curse."

Actual Article Body:
This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten, or redistributed. ©2026 FOX News Network, LLC. All rights reserved. Quotes displayed in real-time or delayed by at least 15 minutes. Market data provided by Factset. Powered and implemented by FactSet Digital Solutions. Legal Statement. Mutual Fund and ETF data provided by LSEG.

The Ottumwa City Council in Iowa opened a meeting with a resident reciting a satanic prayer that ended with the declaration 'Hail Satan' Tuesday.

A city council in Iowa erupted after a resident opened a meeting with a satanic prayer Tuesday.

Before the meeting of the Ottumwa City Council began, former council member Matt Dalbey opened with an invocation to the "dark father" to "embrace the Luciferian impulse to eat from the tree of knowledge" before ending with a "Hail Satan" declaration.

After the council recited the Pledge of Allegiance and took roll, New Life Center Pastor Rick Bick interrupted the meeting to demand pushback against Dalbey's invocation.

LUTHERAN MINISTER AND HOUSE CANDIDATE UNDER FIRE AFTER RECOUNTING HER PART IN SATANIST COUPLE'S WEDDING

A meeting of Ottumwa City Council began with a satanic prayer Tuesday. (AP Photo/John Hanna)

"Let's just reverse this curse that was put on our city. That ending with 'Hail Satan' or 'Hail dark god,' that's not welcome here," Bick insisted.

Though City Council member Cara Galloway told Bick to save his comments for public discussion, Bick demanded immediate action.

"It needs to be done now," Bick said. "I appreciate what Ms. Galloway is saying, but that was a curse put on the city. When he said 'Hail Satan' ... most of you know that, and we need to just stop and reverse it."

In response, Ottumwa Mayor Benjamin Foote requested 30 seconds of silence to allow for prayer or reflection and overruled Galloway's efforts to move forward with the meeting.

Reacting to the controversy, Foote told Fox News Digital, "This is not a reflection of our community. As the mayor of my hometown in Iowa, I know the people of Ottumwa, and the invocation read at the start of Tuesday’s meeting does not represent the faith or the values of families who call this city home."

SWING STATE MAYOR SUED AS CITY’S MUSLIM HOLIDAY DISPLAYS IGNITE RELIGIOUS-FAVORITISM FIGHT

Former council member Matt Dalbey is a member of the Satanic Temple in Iowa, according to the Ottumwa Courier. (Getty Images)

After the meeting concluded, Galloway gave additional comments on the matter, repeating past concerns she had about establishing invocations at city council meetings that could lead to more conflicts.

"Opening with an invocation means allowing viewpoints that may not reflect our own, and responding to someone's invocation is a slippery slope to putting a financial liability on the taxpayers and allowing for others to object or respond," Galloway said.

"And this is exactly why I had concerns about having an invocation when we first talked about it. And I think I even specifically referenced that having someone from the Church of Satan or a prayer about Satan when we talked about that, that this could happen, and we would need to allow it.

"I just want to remind us thatm again, sometimes things are said that we may not agree with ... and while you're allowed to do the moment of silence and that kind of thing too, I think we've opened ourselves up for others to object or respond to others' invocations," she continued.

"And we need to remember that we are up here to be neutral and allow viewpoints because we've opened up invocations."

According to a report by The Ottumwa Courier, the city adopted an invocation policy in January. The policy says it does not endorse any faith or religious denomination but is intended "to acknowledge and express the City Council's respect for the diversity of both organized and unorganized religious denominations, as well as other faiths, belief systems, or the lack thereof, represented and practiced among the citizens of the City of Ottumwa."

SUPREME COURT SHOWDOWN LOOMS OVER ST MICHAEL STATUE BLOCKED FROM PUBLIC SAFETY BUILDING

Mayor Benjamin Foote denied the invocation represented the people of his Iowa city. (Satanic Grotto/Getty Images)

In a private message, according to the Ottumwa Courier, Dalbey, who is a member of The Satanic Temple of Iowa, said that the prayer is commonly used by the temple "but has nothing to do with the belief in a satanic deity."

In a comment to Fox News Digital, council member Bill Hoffman described leaving the room once the prayer was invoked and returning for the Pledge of Allegiance, though he defended Dalbey's right to say what he believes.

"I'm a Christian man with Christian values. That doesn't mean I don't want to observe his First Amendment right. It just means that I want to use my rights not to observe that," he said.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Hoffman added that he expects the invocation policy to be discussed in the future and that the council did not condone the content.

text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
DHS Mullin Says Socialists Seek Chaos and Demographic Change

The left-wing advocates demanding the abolition of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) are trying to impose socialism via enforced chaos and demographic change, says Homeland Security chief Markwayne Mullin. 
The post DHS Mullin Says Socialists Seek Chaos and Demographic Change appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:

California’s business heavyweights are warning residents that Sacramento politicians are preparing to drop a “tax bomb” on the state — and they’ve released a new ad to make the point.

The “explosive” new spot from the Californians Against Wasteful Spending and Higher Taxes coalition uses a fake bomb-squad raid to warn voters about the hundreds of new state and local taxes expected to appear on November’s ballot.

The coalition, a project of the California Business Roundtable, which represents some of the state’s largest employers, released the ad on social media Wednesday.

The 60-second clip opens with people scrambling into a building as two armed men in “Bomb squad” uniforms rush toward an apparent explosive device.

As the bomb squad closes in, one officer warns that no Californian will escape the blast.

A post shared by Californians Against Wasteful Spending and Higher Taxes (@caagainstwastefulspending)

“Every Californian is going to pay more.”

“With this big of a tax bomb nothing is safe. The entire state could get destroyed.”

The ad mentions that roughly 2 million people have “evacuated” — those who have already left California for states including Texas and Florida in recent years.

The message then identifies the culprit as a “group called the politicians,” accusing them of demanding more taxpayer money for “programs even if they all fail.”

subject: Jewish Former Student Sues New York School, Says Admin Refused to Help While Protesters Shoved, Spat on Her
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Jewish Former Student Sues New York School, Says Admin Refused to Help While Protesters Shoved, Spat on Her

On the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023, Hamas terrorist attack on Israel, a Jewish former student at The New School filed a federal lawsuit against the university, accusing the school of failing to protect her from antisemitic harassment, physical assaults, vandalism, and exclusion from campus spaces.
The post Jewish Former Student Sues New York School, Says Admin Refused to Help While Protesters Shoved, Spat on Her appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
On the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023, Hamas terrorist attack on Israel, a Jewish former student at The New School filed a federal lawsuit against the university, accusing the school of failing to protect her from antisemitic harassment, physical assaults, vandalism, and exclusion from campus spaces.

The Lawfare Project, a legal organization dedicated to protecting the civil and human rights of Jewish people worldwide, together with co-counsel Arnold & Porter Kaye Scholer LLP, filed the lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York on behalf of Sophie Shabot, a Jewish American and Israeli citizen who attended The New School’s Parsons School of Design.

The filing came on the third anniversary of the October 7 terrorist attack, in which more than 1,200 people were murdered and another 251 abducted.

The complaint describes a series of incidents beginning after the attack in which Shabot says she was subjected to antisemitic harassment on campus.

In December 2023, protesters blocked Shabot from entering the University Center while allowing non-Jewish students through, according to the lawsuit. The complaint says she was shoved out of the building, spat on, and screamed at through a bullhorn.

The lawsuit says another confrontation occurred in March 2024 after protesters vandalized and took over a space reserved for a Hillel event featuring an Israeli speaker and prevented Jewish students from entering.

The event was moved to a dean’s office without security, where Shabot and other Jewish students were trapped for roughly 20 minutes while protesters pounded on the door and demanded that they turn over the Israeli speaker, according to The Lawfare Project.

The organization says a New School professor then physically shoved the student guarding the door and that the university shut down the event over safety concerns rather than securing the gathering.

As the Jewish students left, protesters pursued Shabot for blocks while calling her a “baby killer,” “genocidal freak,” “Zio cunt,” and “Zio bitch,” according to the complaint. The Lawfare Project says no student was disciplined over the disruption.

The complaint describes another incident in April 2024 in which a crowd allegedly surrounded Shabot and her friends after hearing them speaking Hebrew, formed a tight circle around them, and drove them from the University Center as a security guard remained silent. Shabot’s desk and workspace were also vandalized, according to the filing.

In fall 2024, a protester threw a bottle toward Shabot’s head while she was sitting outside a campus building, missing her by inches, the lawsuit says.

Shabot repeatedly reported the harassment, confrontations, obstruction, and vandalism to professors, campus security, the Office of Student Conduct, senior administrators, and the Office of the President, often identifying those she said were responsible and supplying photographs and video, according to The Lawfare Project.

Following one incident, Shabot emailed more than 20 administrators, the organization says. Only two responded, with both suggesting that she seek therapy.

The complaint also accuses The New School of accommodating some of the protesters. According to The Lawfare Project, the university’s then-president gave participants in an unauthorized encampment $300 to purchase dinner, publicly praised them, and posed for a photograph that included the student accused of spitting on Shabot.

When protesters prevented Jewish students from entering the University Center, the university offered the Jewish students another entrance rather than removing those blocking them, the lawsuit says.

The Lawfare Project says the experience caused Shabot severe anxiety, panic attacks, and insomnia and impaired both her academic performance and her ability to use the studios and equipment required for her education.

“On the third anniversary of October 7, the deadliest day for Jews since the Holocaust, pro-Hamas rallies have been organized across the country, including at universities, to celebrate the massacre,” Lawfare Project Founder and Executive Director Brooke Goldstein said.

“The hatred unleashed on that day has fallen hardest on Jewish college students, including Sophie, and all too often they have been left to suffer in a hostile environment,” Goldstein continued. “This lawsuit is our response to the tidal wave of Jew-hatred on college campuses as well as The New School’s shameful abdication of its responsibility to protect its Jewish students.”

Goldstein said the organization would “continue to advocate for the rights of Jewish students and ensure that those protections are enforced.”

Ziporah Reich, director of litigation at The Lawfare Project and the attorney who filed the lawsuit, said the university had a legal obligation to provide Shabot with an educational environment free from discrimination and harassment.

“Instead, it looked the other way as she was subjected to appalling verbal and physical assault, exclusion, vandalism, and other forms of abuse simply because she is Jewish,” Reich said.

“Rather than protect Sophie, the administration accommodated those targeting her and left her to endure the consequences,” she continued. “The burden of discrimination should never be placed on the student being targeted. By filing this lawsuit, we intend to hold The New School accountable.”

Shabot said she brought the lawsuit because she wants the university held responsible and hopes it changes its treatment of Jewish students.

“I am bringing this lawsuit because what happened to me should not be allowed to happen without accountability,” Shabot said. “I hope that by speaking out, The New School will be forced to confront what went wrong, change the way it responds when Jewish students are targeted, and make sure that no other student has to endure what I did.”

The lawsuit asserts claims under Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the New York State Human Rights Law, the New York Civil Rights Law, the New York City Human Rights Law, and the New York General Business Law. It also includes breach of contract and negligent infliction of emotional distress claims.

Shabot is seeking compensatory and punitive damages, statutory penalties, attorneys’ fees and costs, and other relief and has demanded a jury trial.

The Lawfare Project said the case follows other cases it says it has won or settled, resulting in changes on American college campuses.

The lawsuit comes as the Department of Education announced on X Wednesday:

“Recently released 2023–24 CRDC data show that Jewish students are the most frequently targeted for religion-based bullying. On the third anniversary of the tragedy of October 7, we encourage teachers, administrators, and state leaders to uphold civil rights protections and ensure every student has a safe learning environment.”

The New School has previously faced criticism over antisemitism on campus and its response to it.

Breitbart News reported in November 2016 that swastikas were found on four dorm-room doors at The New School’s Kerrey Hall in Manhattan. Student Sam Lichtenstein, who lived with three Jewish suitemates, said she broke down in tears after seeing one drawn in black marker on her door’s whiteboard. “It was just heartbreaking,” she said, adding, “We’re just overwhelmed and sad.” Lichtenstein said it was “crazy” for such an incident to happen “in such a progressive city, and a progressive university” while one of her roommates said the graffiti left her in “utter shock.”

In November 2017, Morton A. Klein, national president of the Zionist Organization of America, condemned The New School for hosting an event titled “Antisemitism and the Struggle for Justice” featuring Linda Sarsour and Rebecca Vilkomerson, then the head of Jewish Voice for Peace. In a Breitbart Jerusalem op-ed, Klein criticized both women over their anti-Israel activism, noting that Jewish Voice for Peace promoted anti-Israel boycotts and that Sarsour supported the Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions movement.

He also cited Sarsour’s statement that “there is nothing creepier than Zionism,” her praise for convicted Palestinian terrorist Rasmea Odeh, associations with Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan and Imam Siraj Wahhaj, remarks invoking “jihad” against the Trump administration, past comments about Saddam Hussein, her contention that feminists could not also be Zionists, and several other statements and associations that Klein said made her an inappropriate choice for an antisemitism panel.

A separate Breitbart News report the following day detailed remarks from Susan Shapiro, a self-proclaimed liberal professor at The New School, who said she felt “betrayed” that the school’s Creative Publishing and Critical Journalism program was sponsoring the panel and described Sarsour as a “hatemonger.” Shapiro contrasted the treatment of anti-Israel rhetoric with how she believed similar comments about other groups would be received, writing, “Yet trash-talking Jewish Israelis is not only permitted in progressive circles, it’s rewarded.” She also wrote that “anti-Israel boycotts and bombast clearly mask vitriolic Jew-hatred” and pointed to what she viewed as a double standard in progressive circles.

subject: Rubio at Birthplace of Western Civilization: West Must Rediscover Greatness
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Rubio at Birthplace of Western Civilization: West Must Rediscover Greatness or Face ‘Servitude and Decline’

Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned from the birthplace of Western civilization Wednesday that the West must rediscover the qualities that made it great or resign itself to “atrophy and servitude and decline,” declaring that the choices made over the next decade could determine its course for the next century.
The post Rubio at Birthplace of Western Civilization: West Must Rediscover Greatness or Face ‘Servitude and Decline’ appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned from the birthplace of Western civilization Wednesday that the West must rediscover the qualities that made it great or resign itself to “atrophy and servitude and decline,” declaring that the choices made over the next decade could determine its course for the next century.

Speaking beneath the Acropolis, Rubio traced the West’s inheritance from ancient Greece through Rome and Christendom to the American founding before turning to what he described as its modern retreat: nations ashamed of their achievements, nationalism made a “dirty word,” open borders, outsourced industry, weakened militaries, and sovereignty increasingly surrendered to global bureaucracies.

At the center of Rubio’s argument was the ancient Greek concept of thumos — the spirit of ambition, courage, and pride that he said allowed civilizations not merely to survive, but to strive.

“The thumos, as the ancient Greeks called it — the fire of passion, strength, courage, pride — is the heart of great civilization,” Rubio said. “And without it? Without it, nations lose their will to fight, the will to strive, the will to survive.”

Rubio argued that much of the modern West had lost precisely that quality, becoming ashamed rather than proud of the achievements that distinguished it.

“Over time, we in the West came to feel ashamed of the very things that made us exceptional,” he said. “We felt embarrassed that our achievements set us apart from the rest of the world. Our prosperity somehow became a source of guilt.”

That loss of confidence, Rubio argued, became a rejection of the West’s own national identity and inheritance: nationalism became “a dirty word,” monuments came down, Western history was condemned, and children were taught to be ashamed of the nations they would inherit.

The consequences, he said, were not merely cultural.

“In the process, we opened our borders and outsourced our industry, and allowed our militaries to wither and to decay,” Rubio said.

Rubio said that retreat also came at the expense of national sovereignty, as Western governments increasingly transferred decisions “to global bureaucracies far beyond the reach of our control.”

The resulting vacuum, he argued, was filled by adversaries that grew more assertive, wealthy, and powerful as Western confidence receded.

Rubio warned that those choices have brought the West to a crossroads at which the decisions of the next decade could shape the next century.

“And now, today, we find ourselves at a crossroads,” he said. “Because the next decade and the decisions we make will write the story of the next century.”

“The course we take will determine whether the West maintains its place at the head of the world or resigns itself to a future of atrophy and servitude and decline,” Rubio warned. “We will either choose to act now or lose the choice to act at all.”

Rubio said the United States has already made its choice under President Donald Trump, casting the America First agenda as a reversal of the decline he attributed to open borders, deindustrialization, military weakness, and the surrender of national sovereignty.

“Under President Trump, the United States has made its choice,” Rubio declared. “We choose the unapologetic pursuit of national power: to take back control of our critical supply chains, to reindustrialize our economy, to rebuild our defense, to fight for dominance of the technologies and industries of the future.”

That pursuit, Rubio said, means competing across advanced manufacturing, artificial intelligence, semiconductors, minerals, cyber, energy, and weapons while rebuilding American factories and pushing again into space.

He cast that agenda not as a departure from Western statecraft, but as a return to its classical foundations: diplomacy and prudence backed by military power — and by an adversary’s belief that the West is prepared to use it.

“This is the classical understanding of politics and of statecraft that the Trump Administration hopes to reclaim — reclaim not just for our country, but for the whole of our civilization,” Rubio said.

Having laid out the course he said the United States has chosen under Trump, Rubio urged Europe to undertake a renewal of its own, pointing to rising defense spending, new partnerships, and expanded manufacturing as signs that a broader shift may already be underway.

“We believe that Europe can awaken from its long slumber and rekindle the fire that was lit here millennia ago,” Rubio said.

He held up Greece as “a model ally” on energy, migration, and defense and expressed hope that the rest of Europe would follow its example.

But Rubio made clear that his defense of national sovereignty was not an argument for dismantling the transatlantic alliance. Rather, he argued that an alliance of sovereign nations pursuing common interests would be stronger.

“Though passions may, at times, have strained the bonds of affection between the United States and Europe, it must not be allowed to break them,” he said. “Together, we must strengthen an alliance capable of confronting threats of our age.”

Rubio tied that renewal to a broader defense of national loyalty, rejecting the increasingly fashionable notion, as he put it, that “enlightened foreign policy means prioritizing the global community over one’s own people.”

The ancient Greeks, he said, understood “that there was nothing selfish or wrong about loyalty to your nation, nor anything selfish or wrong about fighting to defend its interests above all else.”

Rubio then drew one of the speech’s sharpest civilizational dividing lines, contrasting the Western ideal of the hero willing to sacrifice his life rather than betray his faith, country, or principles with what he described as the Iranian regime’s glorification of death itself.

“This is wholly different from what we see, even now, for example from fanatics like the radical mullahs of Iran, whose cult of death hails child suicide bombers as national heroes, and portrays martyrdom as an end to itself,” Rubio said.

For Rubio, the dividing line was not simply a willingness to die for a cause, but whether sacrifice flows from a reverence for life and principle or from the worship of death itself.

“Our heroes may be willing to die for their cause; but our heroes do not worship death,” he said. “It is precisely because we value life that we come to recognize the heroism in those who would sooner sacrifice it than to betray their principles.”

Wednesday’s address expanded on a theme Rubio laid out in Munich in February, when he warned that mass migration and globalism threatened the survival of the West and urged Europe to resist what he called the forces of “civilizational erasure.”

From there, Rubio widened the lens again, tracing the Western inheritance from Greece through Rome and Christendom to the American republic — a civilization he described as bound together across centuries by common ideas of truth, duty, excellence, exploration, sacrifice, and national loyalty.

Rubio said confronting today’s challenges requires the West first to recover the civilizational confidence that produced its institutions in the first place.

“Together, we must now rediscover that spirit,” he said. “We are at an inflection point — an inflection point not only in the history of my nation, but an inflection point in the whole of our civilization.”

The stakes, he argued, are no longer theoretical. National interests did not disappear with international institutions, nor did war disappear simply because the West preferred peace. Other powers continued to arm and compete for territory, technology, resources, markets, energy, and influence.

“And now, there is war again. There is new competition between great powers again. There is vulnerability, aggression, terrorism, a whole universe of new threats and attacks again,” Rubio said.

He called for Western institutions and alliances to be rebuilt around what he described as their proper purpose — not erasing the sovereignty or distinct identities of their member nations, but defending them against common threats.

Rubio pointed to U.S.-Greek cooperation in defense, energy, and technology as an example of that approach, along with what he called their “shared ambition to secure Europe’s borders from the threats of mass migration.”

In closing, Rubio returned to the larger inheritance at the heart of his address, arguing that Western renewal begins with recovering pride in the civilization handed down to the present generation rather than apologizing for it.

“It shows us that ours is the inheritance of great heroes, and that we should be proud — that we should be intensely proud — of where we come from,” Rubio said. “We should marvel at what our forefathers carved out of this countryside.”

“The story of our civilization is the greatest story ever known to man. And it began here, with the first men and women of the West.”

“From them,” Rubio concluded, “we can rediscover the virtues, the courage, and the strength to confront the dangers that we face in our time.”
